stemMd: A model is $N(t)=50\cdot3^{t/4}$. Which equivalent form most directly shows the growth factor for each one-unit increase in $t$?
explanationMd: Use the exponent identity 3^(t/4)=(3^(1/4))^t. The one-unit growth factor is the fourth root of 3, while 3 is the factor over four time units.

distractorRationale.a: Dividing an exponent is not the same as dividing the base.
distractorRationale.b: The denominator belongs in the exponent.
distractorRationale.c: This multiplies the base by the time denominator incorrectly.
